candidates.attacker_control: A remote, unauthenticated HTTP/2 peer fully controls the inbound frame stream: it can complete the HTTP/2 connection preface, open a stream, and send an arbitrary number of DATA frames whose payload length is zero and whose END_STREAM flag is unset (9 bytes per frame, no flow-control window consumption).
candidates.counterevidence_checked: 1) Searched case-insensitively for `emptydataframe` across all readable files: only the two class files themselves, no callers. 2) Searched for `decoderEnforce` and `DEFAULT_MAX_CONSECUTIVE`: zero matches, so no setter or default constant exists. 3) Relation index confirms `Http2EmptyDataFrameConnectionDecoder` has only internal edges (constructor/override/containment) and no incoming construction calls, whereas `buildFromConnection` does call `Http2ControlFrameLimitEncoder` (line 499) and `StreamBufferingEncoder` (line 509). 4) Examined `DefaultHttp2ConnectionDecoder.onDataRead` for any alternative empty-frame accounting: none; empty frames reach the application listener. 5) Compared with other wired defenses (`Http2SettingsReceivedConsumer` used by `DefaultHttp2ConnectionDecoder` lines 118-126; `Utf8FrameValidator` added by both WebSocket client/server handlers), confirming the orphaned state is specific rather than a general pattern. 6) `Http2EmptyDataFrameConnectionDecoder`/`Listener` are package-private with no public exposure, so an application cannot enable the protection itself through a builder API.
candidates.impact: Remote denial of service: an attacker can force unbounded per-frame parsing, flow-control bookkeeping, and application-listener callbacks for arbitrarily many 9-byte empty DATA frames on a single connection, without ever consuming the flow-control window that would otherwise throttle data. Netty's own class Javadoc states these classes exist to enforce a limit and tear the connection down; with the wiring absent, that protection never activates for any HTTP/2 endpoint built via the shipped builders (the flood-protection threshold is not even configurable). The defect corresponds to the unprotected state for the HTTP/2 empty-DATA-frame flood vector.
candidates.prerequisites: The application uses Netty's HTTP/2 handlers built through the standard builders (`Http2FrameCodecBuilder`, `Http2ConnectionHandlerBuilder`, `Http2MultiplexCodecBuilder`, or subclasses), which all lead to `AbstractHttp2ConnectionHandlerBuilder.buildFromConnection`; the attacker can reach the HTTP/2 endpoint and keep one connection open.
candidates.root_cause: The repository contains the mitigation pair `Http2EmptyDataFrameConnectionDecoder` + `Http2EmptyDataFrameListener` (which closes the connection with ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM after a bounded number of consecutive empty DATA frames), but the decoder is never instantiated. `AbstractHttp2ConnectionHandlerBuilder.buildFromConnection` (lines 481-515) builds `DefaultHttp2ConnectionDecoder` and passes it directly to `buildFromCodec`; there is no `maxConsecutiveEmptyFrames` field/setter and no `DEFAULT_MAX_CONSECUTIVE_EMPTY_FRAMES` constant in `Http2CodecUtil` (only `DEFAULT_MAX_QUEUED_CONTROL_FRAMES` at line 135), so neither the default path nor any configuration path can enable the limit. The analogous encoder-side flood control (`Http2ControlFrameLimitEncoder`) *is* wired at lines 498-500, showing the omission is specific to the empty-DATA-frame defense.
candidates.title: HTTP/2 empty-DATA-frame flood protection class is never wired into decoder construction
candidates.trace: Inbound bytes -> `DefaultHttp2FrameReader.readDataFrame` computes `dataLength = lengthWithoutTrailingPadding(payloadEndIndex - payload.readerIndex(), padding)` = 0 for an empty frame -> `DefaultHttp2ConnectionDecoder.FrameReadListener.onDataRead` (line 231) -> `bytesToReturn = data.readableBytes() + padding` = 0 and flow-control bookkeeping consumes nothing (lines 235, 281-283) -> application `listener.onDataRead(ctx, streamId, data, padding, endOfStream)` is invoked once per frame (line 292). Nothing in this path counts consecutive empty frames. The only counter implementation is `Http2EmptyDataFrameListener.onDataRead` (lines 38-50, `emptyDataFrames++ == maxConsecutiveEmptyFrames` -> connection error ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM), and `Http2EmptyDataFrameConnectionDecoder.frameListener` (lines 33-40) is the only way to install it; neither class is referenced from any builder or handler (`buildFromConnection` lines 512-514 construct `DefaultHttp2ConnectionDecoder` and never wrap it, and `Http2FrameCodecBuilder.build()` lines 193-196 do the same on its test-only frameWriter path).
candidates.unverified: No upstream diff was available in this run, so I could not prove the wiring was intentionally removed versus an incomplete upstream intermediate commit; the exact intended default threshold (upstream-style value unverified) and the exact builder setter name are unknown. No code was executed, so the DoS is not runtime-confirmed. It is possible an application that supplies its own decoder via `codec(...)` and manually wraps it could re-add the protection, but no such helper or documentation exists here. Whether this rather than the HTTP/1.1 smuggling lead is the dataset's target cannot be established from source alone.
candidates.weakness_type: Missing/disabled security control leading to uncontrolled resource consumption (CWE-693 / CWE-400)

coverage_summary: Scope: 1990 readable files under the assigned source root; binary-like files are refused/skipped, no src/test sources exist in the snapshot (only main sources plus testsuite/src/main and poms), and no file was excluded by size (0 excluded over 5 MiB) or by sensitive-name filters. The P1 relation index reports complete coverage of the same 1990 files (0 missing, 0 hash mismatches) but is navigational only. Review concentrated on network-facing parsing/trust boundaries: buffer/common index checks, codec HTTP/1.1 decoder and multipart decoders, codec-http2 frame reader/decoder/encoder/builders, compression decoders, handler SSL and ipfilter, websocket frame decoding, and the API builders' wiring; the relation index was used to confirm that `Http2EmptyDataFrameConnectionDecoder` has no incoming construction edge. Modules such as resolver-dns, codec-redis/memcache/mqtt/stomp/smtp/socks/dns, transport-native-* C code, and the example/microbench/testsuite trees were only sampled, not exhaustively reviewed; no build or runtime checks were performed.
limitations: No upstream source or patch data was available in this run, so the candidate rests on internal-consistency evidence (unused security classes, missing wiring/config) rather than a verified regression diff.
No code was built, executed, or fuzzed; the DoS impact is argued from source flow, not runtime-confirmed.
Test sources are absent from the snapshot, so test expectations could not be used to confirm the intended default behavior or to discover the target defect.
Only one candidate may be submitted; the HTTP/1.1 request-smuggling leniency, the zlib unbounded-decompression path, and multipart parsing growth remain unselected and were not fully traced.
Large portions of the repository (native C transports, DNS resolver, non-HTTP codecs, example/microbench code) were not exhaustively reviewed, so a stronger defect there cannot be excluded.

rejected_leads.lead: HTTP/1.1 request smuggling via lenient header/framing parsing in codec-http: `HttpObjectDecoder.splitHeader` (lines 720-751) accepts whitespace before the colon and trims trailing whitespace from header values, `HttpUtil.getContentLength` (lines 145-197) parses only the first Content-Length value without rejecting duplicates/conflicts, and `readHeaders` (lines 568-620) lets `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` override a present Content-Length without rejecting the ambiguity.
rejected_leads.reason: This is a genuine parser-differential risk present in this version (it matches the class of later Netty request-smuggling fixes and is not disproved), but exploitation requires a front-end intermediary whose framing interpretation differs from Netty's, and I could not tie it to a snapshot-specific deviation as cleanly as the orphaned HTTP/2 mitigation. Kept as an unconfirmed secondary lead; not submitted due to the one-candidate cap.

rejected_leads.lead: Unbounded decompression in `codec/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/compression/JdkZlibDecoder.java` (`decode`, lines 131-238): the inflated `decompressed` buffer is grown with `ensureWritable(inflater.getRemaining() << 1)` and emitted without any maximum-output limit, allowing a small compressed payload to expand until allocation fails.
rejected_leads.reason: Reachable only when a Zlib/Gzip decoder is explicitly added to a pipeline and impact is availability-only DoS; the missing cap is arguably by design in this version and I could not establish that it is the snapshot-specific defect. DoS-only and weaker evidence than the candidate above.

rejected_leads.lead: Memory-growth/DoS paths in `HttpPostMultipartRequestDecoder` (undecodedChunk handling and delimiter scanning) and other lenient multipart parsing.
rejected_leads.reason: Not traced to a concrete attacker-controlled unbounded allocation within the review budget; no source-level proof of an exploitable limit circumvention was established. Rejected as unverified.

summary: Reviewed the Netty 4.1.39.Final-SNAPSHOT source tree (1990 readable files, main sources only; no src/test present; binary files skipped). Strongest candidate: the HTTP/2 empty-DATA-frame flood protection is present as dead code. `Http2EmptyDataFrameConnectionDecoder`/`Http2EmptyDataFrameListener` exist (added for the empty DATA frame flood class of DoS), but no code path ever constructs them: `AbstractHttp2ConnectionHandlerBuilder.buildFromConnection` (lines 481-515) returns a plain `DefaultHttp2ConnectionDecoder` without wrapping, `Http2CodecUtil` has only `DEFAULT_MAX_QUEUED_CONTROL_FRAMES` (no consecutive-empty-frame default), and there is no `maxConsecutiveEmptyFrames` field, setter, or builder API anywhere (zero matches for `decoderEnforce`, `DEFAULT_MAX_CONSECUTIVE`, `EmptyDataFrame` uses). Because empty DATA frames consume no flow-control window and are forwarded to the application listener (`DefaultHttp2ConnectionDecoder` lines 290-293), a remote unauthenticated HTTP/2 peer can drive per-frame processing indefinitely, which is exactly the vector the orphaned classes were written to stop. I selected this over the also-present HTTP/1.1 request-smuggling leniency (HttpObjectDecoder/HttpUtil), which depends on a non-conforming intermediary, and over the zlib-bomb lead.
